title: BANZA Protocol — Canonical Invariant Registry
description: The single machine-readable source of truth for every financial, trust, and structural invariant of the BANZA protocol. Each invariant is defined once here with a canonical ID, its normative statement, and the authoritative source of that statement. Contracts (contracts/**) and the conformance suite (conformance/**) may only cite invariant IDs that appear here — as a canonical `id` or as a registered `alias`. A repository guard enforces this: any cited ID absent from this registry fails the build. Canonical IDs are the IDs used by the authoritative definition of each invariant; `aliases` capture family shorthands that appear elsewhere in the protocol (e.g. the `INV-SETTLE-*` / `INV-RECON-*` family names advertised in README and CLAUDE.md map to the settlement `INV-STL-*` and federation-reconciliation `INV-FED-RECON-001` invariants that actually carry the normative text).
canonical_source: This registry. Prose definitions in docs/reference/en/complete.md, spec/invariants.md, spec/federation/FEDERATION_INVARIANTS.md, docs/governance/BANZA_TRUST_ARCHITECTURE.md, and the referenced ADRs remain the human-readable elaboration; where a statement here and a prose doc disagree, this registry's `statement` plus its cited `source` govern.

severity_levels.critical: A violation creates, destroys, or misattributes value, or breaks the trust anchor. Blocks conformance unconditionally.
severity_levels.high: A violation breaks an integrity or safety guarantee without necessarily creating value directly. Blocks conformance at the level where the capability is declared.
severity_levels.medium: A violation degrades auditability or interoperability. Conditional finding.

families.LEDGER: Double-entry ledger integrity — balance, immutability, integer precision, atomicity.
families.WALLET: Wallet balance integrity — ledger-derived, non-negative, reserved/available identity.
families.SETTLE: Settlement correctness — amount identity (gross=net+fee), no negative balances, immutable batches. Canonical IDs use the INV-STL-* prefix; INV-SETTLE-* is the advertised family alias.
families.RECON: External reconcilability — posting linkage via trace_id. The core family alias INV-RECON-* maps to the federation-scoped INV-FED-RECON-001.
families.QR: QR payment integrity — single-use, expiry, atomicity, signature, environment binding.
families.TRACE: Causal traceability across the event chain.
families.EVENT: Event stream integrity — id uniqueness, timestamp immutability.
families.MON: Monetary representation — integer minor units across the entire surface.
families.OTE: Open Trust Evaluation (ADR-027) — the general protocol trust model without a CA: signed protocol metadata authenticity, evidence binding and reproducibility, fail-closed on missing/invalid/expired/revoked material, revocation-list validity, and the boundary that no BANZA-issued artifact about an operator and no human decision is an input.
families.FEDEVAL: Federation Trust Evaluation (ADR-031) — the federation-routing application of the Open Trust Evaluation: ten conjunctive, locally-executed, fail-closed checks a routing party runs over a peer's published material.
families.ROOT: Root key, Key Manifest and key-management integrity — signing scope, manifest signature/expiry, key validity windows, threshold root custody, bounded delegation, seat continuity, and authenticated key rotation.
families.FED: Federation correctness — cross-operator trace identity, obligations, idempotency, value conservation, revocation, reconcilability.
families.COLLECTION: Payment collections (splits) — no value holding, amount identity, terminal shares, idempotent creation.

invariants.title: Debits equal credits
invariants.statement: Every ledger posting MUST be perfectly balanced: for each currency present, sum(debits) == sum(credits) in integer minor units. A posting with non-zero net MUST be rejected before it is written to storage.

invariants.title: Ledger immutability
invariants.statement: Ledger entries are append-only. Once posted, a posting and its entries MUST never be modified or deleted. Corrections are made only by posting reversing entries.

invariants.title: Integer amounts
invariants.statement: All ledger amounts are integers in minor units (i64) — never floating point.

invariants.title: Atomic postings
invariants.statement: A posting is atomic: partial postings never persist. Either all entries of a posting are committed or none are.

invariants.title: No double settlement
invariants.statement: Each transfer appears in exactly one settlement batch. A transfer MUST NOT appear in multiple settlement batches; operators MUST track settled transfers and reject re-settlement.

invariants.title: Balance identity
invariants.statement: For every wallet at all times: balance_minor = available_minor + reserved_minor. Wallet balances are derived from the ledger — there is no separate balance column that can diverge — and available balance MUST never go below zero.

invariants.title: Settlement amount identity (no money creation)
invariants.statement: For every settlement: gross_minor = net_minor + fee_minor, exact in integer minor units. No money may be created or destroyed by settlement.

invariants.title: No negative balances
invariants.statement: No settlement operation may drive any wallet or ledger account to a negative balance.

invariants.title: Settlement batch immutability
invariants.statement: Settlement batch amounts (gross, fee, net) are computed at creation time and are immutable thereafter; each batch covers a specific, non-overlapping period and follows the lifecycle PENDING -> PROCESSING -> COMPLETED/FAILED.

invariants.title: Idempotency key replay safety
invariants.statement: Every financial write carries a caller-supplied idempotency_key. If the same key is submitted twice, the implementation MUST return the existing result without creating a duplicate. Same key with a different request body MUST be rejected (409 Conflict), never silently served the first response.

invariants.title: Trace propagation
invariants.statement: Every event MUST carry a trace_id and correlation_id. All artefacts in the same causal payment flow MUST share the same trace_id.

invariants.title: Handle uniqueness
invariants.statement: @handle uniqueness is global within an operator's identity namespace; a handle resolves to exactly one wallet identity.

invariants.title: Event id uniqueness
invariants.statement: Event IDs are globally unique. No id value appears twice in the event stream.

invariants.title: Event timestamp immutability
invariants.statement: created_at is set at emission time and is immutable after emission.

invariants.title: Integer-only monetary representation
invariants.statement: All monetary values MUST be integers in minor units. Floating-point monetary values are prohibited across the entire protocol surface: APIs, traces and logs, operator manifests, wallet balances, ledger entries, settlement batches, and SDK contracts. Every monetary field carries the _minor suffix.

invariants.title: Dynamic QR single-use
invariants.statement: A dynamic QR code MUST be paid at most once. A second payment attempt against a USED QR MUST return HTTP 422.

invariants.title: QR expiry rules
invariants.statement: A static QR MUST have expires_at = null. A dynamic QR MUST have expires_at set and in the future at creation time.

invariants.title: Terminal-state rejection
invariants.statement: A QR code in status EXPIRED or USED MUST reject payment.

invariants.title: QR payment atomicity
invariants.statement: The ledger posting and the QR status transition to USED MUST be atomic. Partial state (ledger without status update, or status update without ledger) is a financial-invariant violation.

invariants.title: Dynamic QR signature verification
invariants.statement: A dynamic QR's HMAC signature MUST be verified against the server-side database record before payment. Verifying the payload alone is insufficient.

invariants.title: QR environment prefix binding
invariants.statement: An operator with simulated=true MUST emit BANZA-SBX: prefixed payloads. Emitting the production BANZA: prefix from a sandbox is a conformance FAIL.

invariants.title: Protocol metadata signature validity
invariants.statement: Protocol metadata MUST verify against a delegated signing key endorsed by valid root-signed root metadata, within that key's scope and validity. Unverifiable protocol metadata MUST be treated as absent.

invariants.title: Evidence binds to its manifest
invariants.statement: An Evidence Bundle MUST verify against the public key material bound in the manifest it names, and its manifest_hash MUST bind to that same manifest. Evidence that does not bind to a manifest is not evidence.

invariants.title: Evidence is version- and vector-anchored
invariants.statement: Conformance evidence MUST name a spec version and vector set whose digests match protocol metadata verified under the root-anchored trust chain (signed by a delegated key endorsed by root-signed root metadata). Evidence produced against unknown, unpinned or non-genuine vectors MUST NOT be accepted.

invariants.title: Evidence is reproducible
invariants.statement: Re-executing the named public vectors against the same artifacts MUST reproduce conformance_report_hash. A bundle that does not reproduce is invalid.

invariants.title: Fail-closed on missing or invalid trust material
invariants.statement: Missing, invalid, expired, revoked or incompatible trust material MUST result in non-interoperation. No grace period, no default-allow, no override.

invariants.title: Revocation-list validity
invariants.statement: A Revocation List MUST be signed and unexpired to be relied upon. An unsigned, unverifiable or expired list MUST be treated as unavailable, which is itself fail-closed (INV-OTE-005).

invariants.title: No BANZA-issued artifact is an input
invariants.statement: No artifact issued by BANZA about an operator may be an input to the Open Trust Evaluation. A verifier that requires one is not implementing this protocol.

invariants.title: No human decision is an input
invariants.statement: No human decision may be an input to the Open Trust Evaluation, and no human decision may convert a negative conformance result into a positive one.

invariants.title: Trust root signs nothing about operators
invariants.statement: The Trust Root MUST NOT sign any statement about an operator's identity, status, eligibility or right to participate. The Trust Root signs only the Key Manifest that endorses the delegated signing keys; protocol metadata, releases, the revocation list and conformance evidence are signed by delegated keys within their domains, never by the root directly (INV-ROOT-004; ADR-027).

invariants.title: Fail-closed is not a judgment
invariants.statement: Fail-closed is a decision by the evaluating party about an interaction. It MUST NOT be recorded, published or communicated as a rejection, sanction or judgment about the entity.

invariants.title: Routing requires all checks to pass
invariants.statement: A routing decision MUST NOT be made unless checks 1-9 all pass, evaluated by the deciding party itself over material it verified itself.

invariants.title: Fail-closed on missing, invalid or revoked material
invariants.statement: Missing, invalid, expired, revoked, incompatible or indeterminate trust material MUST fail closed. Absence of an answer MUST NOT be treated as a passing answer.

invariants.title: Conformance evidence is reproducible
invariants.statement: Conformance evidence MUST be reproducible: hashes recomputed from the published artifacts, and the automation re-executed by an independent third party, MUST yield the same state. Evidence that cannot be reproduced is not evidence.

invariants.title: Signed protocol metadata verifies to the trust root
invariants.statement: Signed protocol metadata MUST verify to the trust root through in-scope, unexpired, unrevoked delegated keys. Unsigned or unverifiable protocol material MUST NOT be used as the basis of an evaluation.

invariants.title: Revocation list signed and fresh
invariants.statement: The revocation list MUST be signed and within its freshness window. An unavailable, unsigned, unverifiable or stale list MUST be treated as untrusted material — never as an empty list.

invariants.title: Freshness window, no grace period
invariants.statement: Trust material outside its declared freshness window MUST be rejected. No grace period is permitted. The effective trust lifetime is the minimum of the windows in play (≤ 90 days for L3+).

invariants.title: Capability compatibility requires covering evidence
invariants.statement: Capability compatibility MUST be evaluated per capability and per protocol version. A capability declared without covering evidence MUST NOT be routed to. An operator MUST NOT declare supports_federation without published, valid, fresh, non-revoked L3+ conformance evidence.

invariants.title: No human, issued-artifact or registry-listing step
invariants.statement: No evaluation step may be satisfied by a human decision, by an artifact issued to an operator by BANZA, or by the presence of an entry in the Public Protocol Registry. Registry listing is not a check.

invariants.title: Trust root does not sign operator evidence
invariants.statement: The trust root MUST NOT sign operator conformance evidence. Operators sign their own evidence with their own keys.

invariants.title: Revocation is a security signal only
invariants.statement: Revocation MUST be applied as a cryptographic security signal only. It MUST NOT be represented or used as a regulatory sanction, a licence withdrawal, or a judgment about an entity.

invariants.title: No test key IDs in production
invariants.statement: Production key IDs MUST NOT start with 'test-'. Test keys are rejected in production.

invariants.title: Key Manifest is root-signed
invariants.statement: The Key Manifest MUST be signed by the root key. An unsigned or unverifiable manifest is invalid and MUST be rejected. The root signature on the manifest is the sole basis for trusting any issuing key.

invariants.title: Key Manifest expiry
invariants.statement: An expired Key Manifest is invalid. Verifiers MUST detect and reject a stale manifest.

invariants.title: Root signs only manifests
invariants.statement: The root key signs only Key Manifests. It never signs protocol metadata, conformance evidence, or revocation lists directly.

invariants.title: BRL signing authority
invariants.statement: The BRL MUST be signed by the designated BRL-issuing (revocation-domain) key.

invariants.title: Key validity maxima
invariants.statement: Issuing keys have a maximum validity of 184 days; the root key has a maximum validity of 24 months.

invariants.title: No single-entity root control
invariants.statement: No operator, server, domain, participant, or individual entity may solely control the maximum authority of the BANZA protocol. Root custody requires threshold control: three independent root signing authorities, any two of which authorise a root action.

invariants.title: Delegated authority is bounded
invariants.statement: No delegated signing key may exercise authority beyond the scope the active Trust Root explicitly delegates to it. Verification MUST check both that the signature is valid and that the signed artifact falls within the key's delegated scope, resolved from the active Trust Root / Key Manifest and never self-asserted.

invariants.title: Institutional seat continuity
invariants.statement: The loss or replacement of an institutional seat occupant cannot compromise the continuity of the protocol's maximum authority.

invariants.title: Authenticated key rotation
invariants.statement: A key rotation MUST be authenticated by signing the rotation request with the currently-bound private key. Key rotation authenticated by any other means is invalid.

invariants.title: Trace identity across boundaries
invariants.statement: A federation transaction MUST carry the same trace_id in every artefact it produces on both the originating and receiving operator.

invariants.title: Obligation per routing request
invariants.statement: Every accepted cross-operator routing request MUST produce exactly one InteropObligation in the originating operator. No accepted routing request may exist without a corresponding obligation.

invariants.title: Federation capability integrity
invariants.statement: A federation member MUST NOT declare supports_federation: true unless it can actually service federation routing requests at the declared interop_endpoint.

invariants.title: Cross-operator routing idempotency
invariants.statement: Cross-operator routing MUST be idempotent. The same routing_request_id MUST produce the same result regardless of how many times it is submitted.

invariants.title: Value conservation
invariants.statement: No money may be created or destroyed in a federation transaction. The total value deducted from the payer's wallet on Operator A MUST equal the total value credited to the payee's wallet on Operator B.

invariants.title: Trust-material freshness is mandatory
invariants.statement: Trust material MUST expire. Perpetual trust is forbidden. Signed protocol metadata and conformance evidence without an expiry are structurally invalid.

invariants.title: Revoked operator excluded
invariants.statement: A revoked operator MUST be rejected from all routing decisions immediately upon BRL propagation (within 6 hours).

invariants.title: Cross-operator double-entry
invariants.statement: For every cross-operator payment, the combined ledger entries across both operators MUST sum to zero: the DEBIT on Operator A's settlement account and the CREDIT on Operator B's settlement account are the cross-operator counterparts.

invariants.title: Cross-operator integer arithmetic
invariants.statement: All monetary values in federation artefacts MUST use integer minor units. No floating-point representation at any stage of cross-operator communication.

invariants.title: Federation idempotency scope
invariants.statement: Federation idempotency keys (routing_request_id) are globally unique across all operators and all time. No two routing requests from any operator may share a routing_request_id.

invariants.title: Cross-operator reconcilability
invariants.statement: Every cross-operator payment MUST be traceable from Operator A's ledger entry through the obligation to Operator B's ledger entry via the shared trace_id, and MUST be independently auditable without cooperation from either operator.

invariants.title: Collections never hold value
invariants.statement: A Collection never holds or moves value; it has no balance and produces no ledger posting.

invariants.title: Closed-rule amount identity
invariants.statement: For closed rules (EQUAL_SPLIT, FIXED_AMOUNTS, PERCENTAGE), the sum of share amount_minor MUST equal total_amount_minor exactly in integer minor units.

invariants.title: Exact divisibility
invariants.statement: EQUAL_SPLIT with divisibility=EXACT rejects a non-divisible total; there is no silent rounding.

invariants.title: Collected-amount identity
invariants.statement: collected_amount_minor MUST equal the sum of shares whose status is PAID.

invariants.title: Share payment via real transfer
invariants.statement: A share reaches PAID only via a real confirmed Transfer; transfer_id is set and the Transfer's causation_id equals the share's payment_intent_id (per INV-TRACE-001).

invariants.title: Terminal PAID share
invariants.statement: A PAID share is terminal; it MUST NOT accept further payment (no double payment).

invariants.title: Post-OPEN immutability
invariants.statement: After a Collection is OPEN, its currency, rule, and (for closed rules) total_amount_minor are immutable.

invariants.title: Idempotent creation and payment
invariants.statement: Collection creation and share-payment are idempotent on the supplied idempotency key.
